fixed.how: New packages/runtime/src/conversation/recall.ts with two tools, recall {words, also, kinds, from, to, project} and recall_open {ref}. Their definitions are RECALL_DESCRIPTION and RECALL_OPEN_DESCRIPTION, word for word as agreed. They are registered with the four read tools on every turn; the list is sorted by name, so the order is fixed. A turn's RecallScope holds the candidates (read once per turn), the references r1 to r8 (valid in that turn only) and the records opened. A search returns at most 8 hits within 1,500 tokens and an open at most 2,000, measured with the provider's counter on the wrapped text. Each hit reads 'r<n> [kind, local date, project, strong|weak] title: snippet (who)', followed by a 'Looked through: … , 2 to 8 Nov.' line and a line naming any limit that was reached. No result carries an id or text shaped like a credential. Every result is marked untrusted (agent_output with origin record:recall or record:<kind>; documents are repo_file), so the hooks wrap and scan it and noteRecordsRead makes every later change in the turn be read back. agent.ts adds CHAT_RECALL_RULES (exact agreed text) after CHAT_RETRIEVAL_RULES, CHAT_MAX_MODEL_CALLS 6 (was 4) and CHAT_TURN_CALL_ROOM 5 (was 3); the USD 0.25 ceiling stays and a Haiku turn keeps USD 0.05 (tested). conversation-agent.md is now 1.3.0 with a 'What you look up' section, 'Say where an answer comes from in a few words ("in the session of 3 Nov")' and 'If nothing you were given or looked up holds the answer, say what you looked through.'

not_done.problem: L3-left-5: after a cancelled task's pull request is closed on GitHub, the chat's '# Your files' still says it was 'Left open on GitHub when their task was cancelled'.
not_done.why: d1109-chat-guard's rule (no chat turn waits on GitHub) means the per-turn facts read only the app's own records. A cancelled task's pull request usually has no merge record, and nothing stores its state once it is closed on GitHub: the Overview asks GitHub on every read and caches nothing. Following that state needs either a per-turn GitHub call (refused by D3-5) or a stored state written by the merge watcher or the Overview's pull-request read. Those live in loop/merge.ts and pull-requests.ts, which are not this area's (pull-requests.ts is d1109-onerepo-link's in C2). files_list already checks GitHub on demand and says which pull requests are no longer open. Suggested fix for a later area: when the watcher polls, record a cancelled task's closed pull request (for example a field on the task or merge record), and have project-facts read it.

not_done.problem: CR-9's bound 'a status question sends at most 700 more input tokens than at the base'.
not_done.why: The texts this area must ship word for word (CHAT_RECALL_RULES and the two definitions) cost about 640 tokens on the stand-in's counter (characters / 4), and their JSON schemas about 150 more. 700 is therefore impossible with the agreed texts. The schemas were cut where possible (date patterns are checked in code instead) and the prompt's lookup section kept to five lines. Measured: the base request was 8,148 tokens and this branch's is about 9,200, roughly +1,050. The test asserts the status turn adds only those texts, their schemas and the prompt's lookup lines (fixed + 160, and at most 1,000 in all), runs no lookup, and needs one model call. The session lead decides whether to accept it or to shorten the agreed texts.
